broker.name: Interactive Brokers (IBKR)
broker.tagline: A large, low-cost global broker giving access to stocks, options, futures, forex and bonds on exchanges worldwide from one account.
broker.about: Interactive Brokers is a US-based brokerage founded in 1978 and listed on the Nasdaq under the ticker IBKR. It's known for low commissions, very wide market access and professional-grade tools, which makes it popular with active traders. Beginners can open an account with no minimum deposit, but the main desktop platform (Trader Workstation) has a steep learning curve, so many newer users start with the simpler mobile or web apps. Which IBKR company you sign up with, and so which regulator protects you, depends on the country you live in.
broker.regulators_note: You're placed with an IBKR company based on where you live. Check which one your account is opened with, as investor protection rules differ between them.

plans.name: IBKR Pro
plans.billing_note: Pay-per-trade commissions on everything, with the lowest margin rates and IBKR's best order routing. Choose Fixed or Tiered pricing.

plans.name: IBKR Lite
plans.billing_note: Commission-free US stocks and ETFs, but higher margin rates. US stock pricing shown is for US residents.

rows.label: IBKR Pro — Fixed
rows.note: Minimum $1.00 and maximum 1% of trade value per order, plus regulatory fees.

rows.label: IBKR Pro — Tiered
rows.note: Cheaper the more shares you trade each month. Minimum $0.35 per order, maximum 1% of trade value, plus exchange, clearing and regulatory fees.

rows.label: IBKR Lite
rows.note: US residents only, plus regulatory fees.

rows.label: IBKR Pro
rows.note: Depends on monthly volume and the option's premium. Minimum $1.00 per order, plus exchange, clearing and regulatory fees.

rows.label: IBKR Lite
rows.note: Minimum $1.00 per order. US residents only.

rows.label: IBKR Pro
rows.note: $0.85 for your first 1,000 contracts each month, falling with volume. Exchange and regulatory fees are charged on top.

rows.label: Commission
rows.note: 0.20 bp (0.002%) for most people, lower only at very high monthly volume. Minimum $2.00 per order. Exchange and regulatory fees included.

rows.label: Spreads
rows.note: IBKR passes on the prices it gets from big banks without marking them up, and charges the separate commission above instead. Real spreads widen in fast or quiet markets.

broker.costs_note: US pricing shown. Commissions on other countries' markets are different — see IBKR's pricing pages.

leverage.note: Standard US margin rules (Reg T) let you borrow up to half the cost of a stock. Some account types can get more intraday.
Set by the regulator for your IBKR company. Minor pairs and exotic currencies get less.
Each contract has a margin requirement set by its exchange, which IBKR can raise.

broker.leverage_summary: Up to 50:1 on US forex majors
broker.leverage_note: Leverage makes losses bigger as well as gains, and on a margin account you can lose more than you deposited. IBKR can raise its margin requirements at any time.

margin_rates.note: Yearly interest on money borrowed in USD. Rates follow a benchmark interest rate (Pro: benchmark + 0.5% to 1.5%, Lite: benchmark + 2.5%), so they change over time.

other_fees.label: Withdrawals
other_fees.note: After that, a USD bank wire costs $10.00 and an ACH transfer $1.00.

other_fees.label: Market data
other_fees.note: Delayed prices are free. Live data for many exchanges is a paid monthly subscription.

_notes.source: interactivebrokers.com pricing pages (commissions-stocks, commissions-options, commissions-futures, commissions-spot-currencies, margin-rates, other-fees); Trustpilot. Leverage limits are regulatory caps, not checked against IBKR's own margin tables (the forex margin page was unavailable).
